AbsoluteLimitSchema.description: A ceiling expressed in the channel's own unit.
AbsoluteLimitSchema.title: AbsoluteLimitSchema

AbsoluteRangeSchema.description: A target expressed as an absolute range in the channel's unit.
AbsoluteRangeSchema.title: AbsoluteRangeSchema

AnchorSource.description:
Who appended the version. Distinct from :class:`Provenance`.

Provenance is about the *value*; source is about the *writer*, and the
agent may never disguise itself as the athlete (build plan §0.7).
AnchorSource.title: AnchorSource

AnchorType.description:
Anchor quantities the application knows about.

``CP`` and ``W_PRIME`` are reserved by the build plan: the critical-power
model is out of MVP scope, but the enum member exists so adding it later
is not a migration of stored values. Nothing produces or consumes them
yet, and :func:`app.domain.zones.zones_for` rejects them.
AnchorType.title: AnchorType

AnchorUnit.description: Units an anchor value can be expressed in.
AnchorUnit.title: AnchorUnit

AnchorVersionCreate.description: Payload for appending a version to an anchor's history.
AnchorVersionCreate.title: AnchorVersionCreate

AnchorVersionRead.description: One anchor version as returned by the API.
AnchorVersionRead.title: AnchorVersionRead

AthleteRead.description:
The athlete profile as returned by the API.

Every field is nullable: the profile is bootstrapped empty on first access
and filled in from the UI.
AthleteRead.title: AthleteRead

AthleteUpdate.description:
Payload for partially updating the profile.

Omitted fields are left unchanged; an explicit ``null`` clears a field
(for ``sex``, ``capabilities`` and ``plan_state``, "clear" means back to
``unspecified``, ``{}`` and ``active`` — those three have an empty value
rather than an absent one).
AthleteUpdate.title: AthleteUpdate

BandSchema.description: An acceptable range around a step's prescribed target, as fractions.
BandSchema.title: BandSchema

CeilingSchema.description: No more than this long spent above this limit on this channel.
CeilingSchema.title: CeilingSchema

ChannelUnit.description: The unit each channel is measured in.
ChannelUnit.title: ChannelUnit

Discipline.description: The two disciplines the MVP trains.
Discipline.title: Discipline

DurationFloorSchema.description: The session must last at least this long.
DurationFloorSchema.title: DurationFloorSchema

ErrorDetail.description:
Error response body, as produced by the AppError handler.

Reference it in endpoint ``responses={...}`` declarations so error
statuses are part of the OpenAPI contract (and the generated frontend
types).
ErrorDetail.title: ErrorDetail

ExerciseCategory.description:
Movement families the catalogue is organised by.

Patterns rather than muscles: the build plan names squat/hinge/press/pull/
core, and the remaining four cover what a general strength programme needs
without inviting a taxonomy argument.
ExerciseCategory.title: ExerciseCategory

ExerciseRead.description: One catalogue movement as returned by the API.
ExerciseRead.title: ExerciseRead

LoadKind.description:
How the load of a prescribed set is expressed.

Four kinds because four are genuinely different questions: an absolute
weight, a fraction of a one-rep max, a target effort, and "your own body".
Scoring treats them differently — `load_within` tolerance is meaningless
for bodyweight — so the kind is part of the value, not a formatting hint.
LoadKind.title: LoadKind

LoadSchema.description: How heavy a prescribed set is.
LoadSchema.title: LoadSchema

LoadWithinSchema.description: Loads used within this relative tolerance of what was prescribed.
LoadWithinSchema.title: LoadWithinSchema

MetricExplanationRead.description: Why a computed number is the number. Travels with it; not page copy.
MetricExplanationRead.title: MetricExplanationRead

PercentLimitSchema.description: A ceiling expressed as a fraction of an anchor.
PercentLimitSchema.title: PercentLimitSchema

PercentOfAnchorSchema.description: A target expressed as a fraction range of an anchor.
PercentOfAnchorSchema.title: PercentOfAnchorSchema

PinnedAnchorRead.description:
One anchor version this session's percentages resolve against.

The pin is the product's most distinctive invariant (build-plan invariant
4, D49) and it is worth nothing invisible: showing the provenance is what
makes an `estimated` FTP read as an estimate rather than a fact.
PinnedAnchorRead.title: PinnedAnchorRead

PlanState.description:
Whether the plan is being enforced.

``PAUSED`` does not pause the application: see the module docstring for
what it does and does not stop.
PlanState.title: PlanState

PlanWeekDayRead.description: One day of the week, with the sessions planned for it.
PlanWeekDayRead.title: PlanWeekDayRead

PlanWeekDisciplineRead.description:
One week's totals for one discipline.

The two axes keep their own columns. ``planned_load`` is TSS and
``total_sets`` counts strength sets; there is deliberately no field that
could hold their sum, because they measure different things (spec v2
§5.4, §8.3).
PlanWeekDisciplineRead.title: PlanWeekDisciplineRead

PlanWeekRead.description: Seven consecutive days of the plan, empty days included.
PlanWeekRead.title: PlanWeekRead

PlannedSessionCopy.description: Payload for copying a planned session onto another date.
PlannedSessionCopy.title: PlannedSessionCopy

PlannedSessionMove.description: Payload for moving a planned session to another date.
PlannedSessionMove.title: PlannedSessionMove

PlannedSessionRead.description:
One planned session, with the intent version in force.

The three resolved fields are computed on every read from the intent's
frozen prescription and the anchor versions it pinned — never stored, so
appending a new anchor cannot change what an existing session says.
PlannedSessionRead.title: PlannedSessionRead

PlannedSessionUpdate.description:
Payload for updating a planned session. Omitted fields are unchanged.

Touching ``purpose``, ``intent_text``, ``coach_notes``,
``success_criteria``, ``workout_id`` or ``structure`` appends a new intent
version. Touching only ``date`` or ``status`` does not.
PlannedSessionUpdate.title: PlannedSessionUpdate

PredictedLoadRead.description: What this prescription is expected to cost, and how that was arrived at.
PredictedLoadRead.title: PredictedLoadRead

Provenance.description:
Where an anchor value came from — ordered weakest to strongest.

The order matters: it is what later work packages compare when deciding
whether a new value should displace the one in use.
Provenance.title: Provenance

Purpose.description: Why a session exists. One vocabulary, two disciplines.
Purpose.title: Purpose

PurposeTemplateRead.description: One purpose, with what it starts with and how it is judged.
PurposeTemplateRead.title: PurposeTemplateRead

PurposeTemplatesRead.description: The whole vocabulary, in the order the build plan states it.
PurposeTemplatesRead.title: PurposeTemplatesRead

RampStepSchema.description: Move from one set of targets to another over a duration or distance.
RampStepSchema.title: RampStepSchema

ResolvedStepRead.description: One flattened step of the prescription, with its targets resolved.
ResolvedStepRead.title: ResolvedStepRead

ResolvedTargetRead.description:
One channel's target, said both ways.

The prescription and the numbers are both returned because they are both
the truth: ``88–93 % FTP`` is what survives an FTP change and what a
purpose template can express, ``220–232 W`` is what the athlete rides.
ResolvedTargetRead.title: ResolvedTargetRead

ScoringAxis.description:
The axes WP-7 scores a session on.

Named here rather than in WP-7 because the templates reference them, and
the templates are written now. ``RESPONSE`` and ``FUELLING`` are in the
vocabulary but out of MVP scope: WP-7 returns ``not_assessed(deferred)``
for them, so the shape exists without the behaviour.
ScoringAxis.title: ScoringAxis

SessionIntentRead.description:
One version of a planned session's intent.

Carries WP-1's versioning vocabulary verbatim, because it is one of the
versioned artefacts invariant 1 describes.
SessionIntentRead.title: SessionIntentRead

SessionIntentsRead.description: Every intent version of one session, oldest first.
SessionIntentsRead.title: SessionIntentsRead

SessionStatus-Input.description:
Where a planned session ended up.

``DISPLACED`` is not ``MISSED``: the athlete trained, just not this. WP-6
sets it when a low-similarity activity is deliberately linked; the member
exists now so the column does not need a migration then.
SessionStatus-Input.title: SessionStatus

SetsCompletedSchema.description: At least this fraction of the prescribed strength sets performed.
SetsCompletedSchema.title: SetsCompletedSchema

Sex.description:
Biological sex, as it affects physiological reference values.

``UNSPECIFIED`` is a real member rather than ``None`` so the column is
never null and reads state "not answered" instead of "unknown why".
Sex.title: Sex

StalenessState.description:
How much an anchor version is still to be trusted.

The staleness *model* is deferred past the MVP, but the field is not:
every version stores one, hardcoded to ``FRESH`` today (see
:data:`MVP_STALENESS_STATE`). ``AGING`` and ``STALE`` are reserved so that
turning the model on later is code, not a data migration.
StalenessState.title: StalenessState

SteadyStepSchema.description: Hold a set of targets for a duration or a distance.
SteadyStepSchema.title: SteadyStepSchema

StepRole.description:
What a step is for within the session.

Roles are what a success criterion selects on (``time in band across the
work steps``) and what WP-5's alignment matches against, so they are part
of the prescription rather than a display hint.
StepRole.title: StepRole

StepSelectorKind.description: How a criterion picks the steps it applies to.
StepSelectorKind.title: StepSelectorKind

StepSelectorSchema.description: Which flattened steps a criterion applies to.
StepSelectorSchema.title: StepSelectorSchema

StrengthGroupSchema.description: One or more lines performed together; more than one is a superset.
StrengthGroupSchema.title: StrengthGroupSchema

StrengthSetSchema.description: One line of a strength prescription.
StrengthSetSchema.title: StrengthSetSchema

TimeInBandSchema.description: At least ``min_fraction`` of the selected steps' time inside the band.
TimeInBandSchema.title: TimeInBandSchema

ValidationErrorDetail.description:
422 response body — the one status with two shapes.

A service raising :class:`ValidationError` produces a sentence; FastAPI's
own request validation produces its list of per-field errors. Both are
422s on the same endpoint, so the declared contract has to admit both, or
a schema-conformance fuzzer is right to call one of them a lie.
ValidationErrorDetail.title: ValidationErrorDetail

WeekSessionRead.description: One planned session, as a calendar card shows it.
WeekSessionRead.title: WeekSessionRead

WorkoutCreate.description: Payload for adding a workout to the library.
WorkoutCreate.title: WorkoutCreate

WorkoutLabelsRead.description: The folder labels and tags currently in use across the library.
WorkoutLabelsRead.title: WorkoutLabelsRead

WorkoutRead.description: One library workout as returned by the API.
WorkoutRead.title: WorkoutRead

WorkoutSummarySchema.description: Derived facts about a prescription. Computed on read, never stored.
WorkoutSummarySchema.title: WorkoutSummarySchema

WorkoutUpdate.description: Payload for partially updating a workout. Omitted fields are unchanged.
WorkoutUpdate.title: WorkoutUpdate

ZoneModel.description:
The zone schemes the MVP supports.

One per channel: power zones off FTP, heart-rate zones off LTHR. Adding a
model is adding a member plus a row in :data:`_ZONE_SCHEMES`.
ZoneModel.title: ZoneModel

ZonesRead.description:
The computed zones, with the two inputs they came from.

The anchor version is returned in full because it is the provenance of
every number in ``zones``; a client that caches the zones caches the
version id with them.
ZonesRead.title: ZonesRead

app__api__schemas__auth__SessionStatus.title: SessionStatus

app__domain__sessions__SessionStatus.description:
Where a planned session ended up.

``DISPLACED`` is not ``MISSED``: the athlete trained, just not this. WP-6
sets it when a low-similarity activity is deliberately linked; the member
exists now so the column does not need a migration then.
app__domain__sessions__SessionStatus.title: SessionStatus

get.description: Get one planned session with the intent version in force.

patch.description:
Update a planned session, appending an intent version if intent changed.

Editing intent before the session has been matched re-pins its anchors;
editing it afterwards keeps the pins, flags the new version
`edited_post_hoc`, and triggers a rescore (build-plan invariant 4).

422.description: Session violates a schema or domain rule

post.description:
Copy a planned session onto another date.

The copy is a **new** planned session: status `planned`, its own intent
chain starting at version 1, and its anchors pinned at the versions in
force now — a prescription freezes when it is planned, and this one is
being planned now (invariant 4, D57).

422.description: Session violates a schema or domain rule

get.description:
List every intent version of one session, oldest first.

Unpaged: intent versions are the history of one session's prescription,
and there are a handful even for a much-edited one.
Get one intent version — what was prescribed at that point.

post.description:
Move a planned session to another date.

Its own verb rather than `PATCH ... {"date": ...}`, which does the same
thing: dragging a card across the calendar is one intention, and the audit
trail should be able to say so (D56). Nothing about the prescription
changes — no intent version, no re-pinning.

422.description: Session violates a schema or domain rule

get.description: List every purpose with its scoring axes and default success criteria.

Get one purpose's template.

No 404 is declared because none is reachable: the path parameter is the
purpose enum, so an unknown value is a 422 from the parser, and every
known value has a template or the application would not have booted.
